newsitem.title: singapore: Asian crudes stay firm as Gulf trade brisk.
newsitem.headline: Asian crudes stay firm as Gulf trade brisk.

text.p: Crude oil prices in Asia were firmer on Monday with trading of Gulf crudes continuing briskly and at maintained premiums.
India awarded four cargos of Dubai in its December tender supporting Dubai intermonth spreads. It also awarded three VLCCs of Qua Iboe.
December/January Dubai spreads pushed out slightly to 50/57 cents from Friday's 50/55, January/February to 53/60 from 50/55 and February/March to 52/60 from 50/55.
The Brent/Dubai for December was steady at $2.42/$2.55, but January tightened slightly to $2.25/$2.35 from $2.25/$2.40.

As India awarded its December requirements, Thailand's Bangchak refinery tendered to buy 500,000 barrels of Gulf grades and 600,000 barrels of Far East grades. The tender closes on Wednesday and offers should be valid for 24 hours.
In Gulf trading, three Murban cargoes traded at a premium of 55 cents over ADNOC and another at a premium of 61 cents -- the highest for December barrels.
Oman saw a trade between a state oil company and a Japanese trader at MPM +7.5 cents, while two other Oman cargoes were swapped with Umm Shaif barrels at an equivelent price of MPM +5 cents.
Qatar Land was traded several times at a premium of up to 40 cents over QGPC, the highest premium for December to date. Lower Zakum traded at 60 cents over ADNOC, in line with recent deals.
Most of November Tapis is already placed but the paper continued to firm in line with the Brent and NYMEX futures rallies.
November Tapis was bid at $25.35 and December at $25.05, up around 15 cents from Friday's values. A producer was offering December wet barrels at a premium of $1.50.
